summary: Researched the evening before (Sat 14 Nov) under the stricter rules and re-checked this morning with live prices; lineups and NFL inactives are not out, so this is a draft until the final check. Eight well-covered games were researched: five are kept at medium and three at low; the rest were not reached. No favourite's price fell overnight. Medium: Seahawks at Raiders (p 0.69; Seattle start backup QB Lock behind a line missing two starters, the Raiders start a rookie QB for the first time), Texans at Browns (p 0.63; a road favourite without Hunter, Harrison and now Montgomery, a third tackle questionable, Browns 3-0 at home), Bills at Jets (p 0.77; Bills 7-1, right tackle doubtful, 27 mph gusts), Rams at Cardinals (p 0.77; Cardinals start a rookie QB, Rams without Nacua and Adams and lost to them 16-18 in October), France–Türkiye (p 0.79, raised from low: the coach confirmed Mbappé is available and two French outlets give the same probable XI; France need a point, Türkiye are relegated, but France miss about ten players and field a young back line). Low, so not bet: Croatia–Czechia (Croatia's price fell 4.7% in 24 hours with no news, four straight defeats), Finland–San Marino (no team news, near dead rubber, only goals legs near 60%), Zverev–Jodar (form, fitness and a second price not verified). Afternoon check (about 16:40 UTC): the Texans are now low and off the slip, because their inactives list ruled out starting guard Teller on top of Rutledge, Hunter, Harrison and Montgomery and the price fell 3%. Seahawks, Bills and Rams were re-checked with no late news against them and stay medium; the 21:05 UTC games publish their inactives only at 19:35 UTC.

checks.team_news: No injury or suspension report found for Finland or San Marino for this game (Sports Mole previews of earlier group games reported no Finland injuries; no later report found; San Marino squad news not found). Lineups not out; nothing confirmed.
checks.lineups: Not announced. Finland's last published likely XI (Sports Mole, Oct): Hradecky; Stahl, Miettinen, Koski, Lahteenmaki; Kairinen, Markhiev, Kamara; Walta, Pohjanpalo, Keskinen. Starting11 shows only a formation shape for this game, no names. Confirmed XIs due about an hour before the 17:00 UTC kickoff; second source not available.
checks.rotation: Finland played Albania away in Tirana on Thu 12 Nov (3 days earlier) and, per the group table, lost, so little travel but a short turnaround. San Marino lost 0-2 to Belarus on 12 Nov. This is the last Nations League game for both sides, so some rotation by Finland is possible. None confirmed.
checks.motivation: Table (FotMob C1 after 5 games each, incl. 12 Nov): Albania 12, Belarus 10, Finland 7 (W2 D1 L2, 9-4), San Marino 0 (1-18). Finland can reach at most 10 points and trail Belarus on head-to-head (0-0 and 0-1), so they cannot win the group or finish second. San Marino are bottom with 0 points. Both sides are close to a dead rubber, so this is a soft risk, not the hard rule: the favourite is not secured while the opponent needs a result. Finland may want a big goal difference and a good end to the campaign.
checks.form: Finland in this group: 7-0 at San Marino (26 Sep), 0-0 Belarus, 2-1 at Albania per Flashscore/Sports Mole (Walta 2), 0-1 at Belarus (6 Oct), then a loss to Albania on 12 Nov (score not found; the table implies 0-2). So in the four non-San Marino games Finland scored only 2 goals, and 7 of their 9 goals came in the one game against San Marino. Sports Mole lists their all-competitions form as L, L, W, D, W, L. San Marino: 0-7 Finland, 0-3 Albania, 0-4 Belarus, 1-2 Albania, 0-2 Belarus, so 18 conceded in 5 (3.6 per game), but they lost 2-1 and 0-2 in the last two, which is not a collapse each time.
checks.h2h: Finland won 7-0 in Serravalle on 26 Sep 2026 (11v11, VAVEL); 3 wins from the last 3 meetings, no draws. Finland have never been held by San Marino in that run. The 7-0 looks like the top end: a 3-4 goal total is more typical against a side that has also lost 2-1 and 0-2 recently.
checks.odds: DraftKings via ESPN (site.api.espn.com): Finland 1.02, draw 14, San Marino 31 (opening 1.02 / 13 / 41), total line 4.5; de-vigged 0.904 / 0.066 / 0.030. DraftKings has the draw and upset chances higher than Polymarket's 4.3% draw and 1.3% away. Polymarket Finland 24h move 0.950 to 0.945 (-0.5% relative), well inside the 3% threshold and not a concern. Goals legs: Over 3.5 at 0.595 and Under 4.5 at 0.605 (Polymarket); the total line at DraftKings is 4.5, which suggests a high-scoring game is priced.
checks.models: World Football Elo (eloratings.net, via candidates data): Finland 1514, San Marino 818; expected score for Finland 0.99 (a draw counts as half). A bookmaker-free rating confirms a huge gap but cannot say how many goals Finland will score.
checks.venue_weather: Bolt Arena, Helsinki, evening kickoff 17:00 UTC (19:00 local) on 15 Nov per MyHelsinki; a normal home venue. No weather forecast found; mid-November Helsinki is cold and could bring wet or poor pitch conditions, unverified.

games.reason: Finland are overwhelming favourites but the win price is too short to bet. The goals legs are the interest: Finland scored 7 against San Marino in September, yet only 2 in their other four group games, and with the group lost they may rotate or play at a lower tempo. San Marino concede a lot (18 in 5) but are not conceding 5 a game to the stronger sides. I shade Over 3.5 down below the market and keep Under 4.5 near the market. The 4+ goals scenario needs Finland to score 4 or 5, which they have done once in five games. Confidence is low: no team news or expected XI could be found for either side, the game is close to a dead rubber for both, and the only legs in range are goals totals priced near 60%.
games.main_risk: For Under 4.5, a repeat 7-0 style rout (Finland 5+ goals) is the main risk. For Over 3.5, a low-tempo dead rubber with a rotated Finland side and a stubborn San Marino defence scoring only 2-3 goals. Lineups unknown; second source for XIs missing.

checks.team_news: Mbappe: Sat 14 Nov eve-of-match press conference, Zidane said he 'sera avec nous' and 'on prefere l'avoir' (CNews dated 2026-11-14; Ouest-France, Footeo, Yahoo Sports headlines the same day). He missed the 12 Nov 1-3 loss at Italy with a hamstring/thigh niggle (Flashscore FR, Footiledefrance), stayed with the group, and trained normally. The 'tendon injury / leaves camp' SoccerNews and beIN items are dated 25 Sep 2026 and are old. The latest source is the 14 Nov press conference, so he is available but unconfirmed as a starter until the XI is out. France absences (Flashscore FR, 15 Nov): Dembele, Saliba, Koundé, Kalulu, Lacroix, Tchouameni, Kone, Akliouche, Ekitike, Thuram and Lepaul out; Upamecano left the squad for personal reasons (not an injury, per Haber7 via federation). Konate is back in the probable XIs. His September knee sprain is old news, and I did not find a Nov fitness report. Tchouameni and Thuram out, as before. Turkiye (Flashscore FR, 15 Nov): Kenan Yildiz and Aral Simsir injured, Ozan Kabak suspended, Kahveci and Akturkoglu not in the squad, Bardakci back from suspension. Calhanoglu and Arda Guler appear in the Flashscore FR projected XI, but I did not find a Turkish press source for this window, and Flashscore FR names Sergen Yalcin as coach while September sources name Montella. That coach name conflicts and is unverified. TFF squad news was not read.
checks.lineups: Two French outlets, both projections (no official XI yet): Flashscore FR (4-2-3-1) Maignan; Diouf, Jacquet, Konate, Truffert; Da Cunha, Camavinga; Olise, Cherki, Doue; Mbappe. Footiledefrance (15 Nov, 4-3-3) Maignan; Diouf, Jacquet, Konate, Truffert; Zaire-Emery, Da Cunha, Camavinga or Cherki; Olise, Mbappe, Barcola. Topmercato has Mbappe marked 'sous reserve'. Replacing Thuram and Tchouameni: Da Cunha plus Camavinga or Zaire-Emery in midfield, and Cherki, Doue or Barcola in attack. Both outlets name Konate at centre-back. This is a rebuilt side with a young back line (Diouf, Jacquet), not the September XI. Turkiye projected (Flashscore FR): Cakir; Zeki Celik, Bardakci, Demiral, Kadioglu; Calhanoglu, Kokcu; Akgun, Guler, Baris Alper Yilmaz; Enes Unal. Topmercato's version is similar (Aydin, Kaplan, Demiral, Kadioglu; Yuksek, Kokcu; Akgun, Guler, Yilmaz; Unal). Neither Turkiye XI is confirmed.
checks.rotation: France lost 1-3 at San Siro on Thu 12 Nov, so this is a 3-day turnaround at home in Bordeaux, and the squad is thinned by many absences, so changes are forced rather than chosen (Diouf, Jacquet, Da Cunha are first-choice-by-necessity). Zidane preparing 'plusieurs changements' (Footiledefrance headline). This is the last group game, so there is no next-match rotation motive. Turkiye lost 1-2 to Belgium on 12 Nov and also play on a 3-day turnaround.
checks.motivation: Group A1 after matchday 5 (ESPN via Flashscore, 365Scores): Italy 10 pts (+5), France 10 (+3), Belgium 9 (+2), Turkiye 0 (-10, relegated). Flashscore FR: a draw is enough for France to reach the quarter-finals. With a defeat France still qualify if Belgium do not beat Italy in Brussels. If Belgium win and France lose, France finish third and face a March play-off against a League B runner-up. A win plus an Italy slip gives first place. I checked the arithmetic: draw puts France on 11 against Italy 10 or 11 and Belgium at most 12, so top two holds. France therefore need a point, and Turkiye have nothing to play for. This is the reverse of the dead-rubber exclusion. The kick-off time of Belgium v Italy was not found (ticket pages say 'to be confirmed'; the match is in Brussels).
checks.form: France: L 1-3 at Italy (12 Nov), W 4-1 v Belgium (5 Oct), D 1-1 v Italy (2 Oct), W 1-0 at Belgium (28 Sep), W 1-0 at Turkiye (25 Sep). 8 for, 5 against; Zidane's first defeat as coach on 12 Nov. Turkiye: five defeats from five (L 1-2 Belgium, L 1-3 Italy, L 0-3 Belgium, L 1-4 Italy, L 0-1 France), 3 for and 13 against. xG not found.
checks.h2h: 25 Sep 2026 in Kocaeli: Turkiye 0-1 France (Mbappe goal), a narrow win on a poor pitch. France won by one goal and Turkiye created little, but the scoreline shows a draw or a one-goal win is the realistic failure path against a bottom side. Not a derby or fierce rivalry.
checks.odds: Morning live Polymarket (coordinator refresh): France 0.8264 / draw 0.1172 / Turkiye 0.0564, up 2.8% on last night's 0.8036. Last night's 24h history was flat at 0.795 to 0.805. DraftKings via ESPN (data.odds, evening): France 1.22 / draw 6.00 / Turkiye 10.00, opened 1.17 / 7.50 / 11.00, de-vigged 75.4 / 15.4 / 9.2. Betclic (Flashscore FR, 15 Nov): France 1.19 / draw 6.00 / Turkiye 8.75, de-vigged about 79.0 / 15.7 / 5.3 after rounding, which is shorter than DraftKings and in line with Polymarket's rise. Fox Sports: France -463 / Turkiye +955. The price has moved toward France, not against, with no adverse news. Bookmaker draw of about 15 to 16% is above Polymarket's 11.7%, so I keep the draw at 14%.
checks.models: World Football Elo read tonight from https://www.eloratings.net/World.tsv: France 2066, Turkiye 1753. With 100 points of home advantage the expected score for France is 0.915, where a draw counts as half. That is a strong bookmaker-free edge for France, consistent with a win chance in the high 70s to low 80s and a draw of 13 to 15%. Source https://www.eloratings.net/ (figures supplied by the coordinator, not re-fetched; my own fetch of the site returned no usable table).
checks.venue_weather: Stade Atlantique (Matmut Atlantique), Bordeaux, normal French home venue (Flashscore FR, Fox Sports). Kick-off Sun 15 Nov 20:45 local (19:45 UTC). No weather forecast or pitch problem found.

games.reason: France are home favourites against a Turkiye side on 0 points, five defeats and already relegated, while France need only a point to stay in the quarter-final top two. Mbappe's availability is confirmed by Zidane on 14 Nov and two French outlets give near-identical projected XIs with Konate, Olise, Camavinga and Mbappe leading, so the two key facts from the earlier pass are now established, with no official XI yet. No hard exclusion applies: verified fixture, normal venue, Zidane appointed before September, not a derby, and the favourite has not secured its aim. I keep p below Polymarket's 82.6% (79%) because France lost 1-3 three days ago, have a long absence list and a young back line, Mbappe is not a confirmed starter, and bookmakers price the draw at 15 to 16%. Draw at 14% is far below the 25% limit for a straight win. The Elo expected score of 0.915 supports the favourite.
games.main_risk: A draw or one-goal result: France won only 1-0 in Turkiye in September, lost 1-3 at Italy three days ago, are missing Tchouameni, Thuram, Dembele, Saliba, Kounde and others, and Mbappe's hamstring niggle could keep him out of the XI or limit his minutes. Turkiye's Turkish-press squad news and the Turkiye coach's name were not verified, and Belgium v Italy kick-off time is unknown.

checks.team_news: Checked Sun 15 Nov ahead of the 18:00 UTC kickoff. The official inactives were NOT out in anything I could read. The Jet Press inactives article says to check back around 11:30 a.m. ET, and ESPN's injury feed still shows Saturday and Sunday-morning designations only. Bills (ESPN): RT Spencer Brown doubtful (ankle, set back in Week 9). Tylan Grable is expected to start at RT again (Jet Press, SI, Buffalo Rumblings). Buffalo Rumblings also expects the doubtful tag to become an out. CB Christian Benford (wrist), CB Jordan Hancock (hamstring, activated from IR Saturday) and S Sam Franklin Jr. (shoulder) are still questionable. WR Tyrell Shavers is out (ACL). Josh Allen is not on the Bills report and has no injury designation anywhere I read. Jets (ESPN): WR Garrett Wilson questionable (concussion, updated 12:14Z Sunday); Jet Press says coach Aaron Glenn expects him to play and clear protocol. WRs Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper Jr., S VJ Payne and CB Nahshon Wright are questionable. LB Trevin Wallace is out. Nothing new has been ruled out or downgraded since the morning research. Benford's and Hancock's availability is still unconfirmed.
checks.lineups: Not official. ESPN lists no QB injury for either side, so Allen is expected to start for the Bills and Geno Smith for the Jets. Allen's start is not formally confirmed until the inactives are out. Buffalo is expected to start Grable at RT in place of Brown. Wilson is expected to play per Glenn but is still questionable. The Bills' CB depth depends on whether Benford and Hancock are active.
checks.rotation: No rotation issue. Bills' last five (ESPN): L 26-29 vs NE, W 37-34 OT at LAR, W 33-30 at LV, W 36-10 vs BAL, W 23-6 at MIN (10 Nov). Short travel (Buffalo to MetLife, same time zone). Jets played at KC on 8 Nov (L 12-35).
checks.motivation: Bills 7-1 and ranked No. 1 in PFF's Week 10 power rankings, chasing the AFC top seed and the AFC East. Jets 2-7 and ranked 26th to 31st, playing for pride. No dead-rubber concern.
checks.form: Bills: 4 wins in last 5 (points for 29, 37, 33, 36, 23; against 26, 34, 30, 10, 6). Jets: 1 win in last 5, losses to NE, MIA, LV and KC 12-35; their defence has allowed 25+ in four of those five. Unchanged from morning.
checks.h2h: AFC East divisional game, so a soft risk. Bills beat the Jets in the Week 18 2025 finale. The Jets are at their own MetLife Stadium and Buffalo is the visitor, although the Polymarket listing labels the Bills as home.
checks.odds: Live Polymarket Bills 78.5% (p_first 79.5%, -1.3% relative, about 1 point). The move is small, below the 3% drop threshold, and not adverse enough to matter. DraftKings via ESPN now: Bills -8.5 (-105), total 50.5, moneyline Bills -485 / Jets +370. The opening line was Bills -7 (-110), moneyline -340. The line has moved toward the Bills by 1.5 points of spread and 145 cents of moneyline since open. De-vigged DK is about 79.6% Bills / 20.4% Jets (implied 82.9% and 21.3%). The live Polymarket price is about 1 point below de-vigged DK, so odds and market roughly agree, and DK is stronger on the Bills than the earlier morning snapshot (-395).
checks.models: ESPN matchup predictor: Bills 82.6%, Jets 17.4%. PFF Week 10 power rankings have the Bills at No. 1; other rankings put the Jets 26th to 31st. No Elo or DVOA figures found.
checks.venue_weather: MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford NJ, outdoors, artificial turf. ESPN forecast unchanged: about 50F, gusts 27 mph, 3% precipitation. Wind can trim passing and kicking, and a banged-up Bills line without Brown makes a one-score game more plausible.

games.reason: Re-check on game day. Official inactives were not yet out, so the key unknowns (Brown out and Grable at RT, Benford, Hancock, Franklin, Wilson) are still unconfirmed. No new bad news was found. Allen has no designation, no one new was ruled out, the DK line moved further toward the Bills (-340 to -485 moneyline, spread -7 to -8.5), and the live Polymarket price is down only 1.3% (0.795 to 0.785). That is within the allowed range and below the 3% low-confidence trigger. Confidence stays medium, not high, because the inactives are not confirmed. p kept at 77/23, below the live market (78.5%) and the de-vigged DK (79.6%), to allow for the OL injury, thin CB group and 27 mph gusts.
games.main_risk: Divisional road game at MetLife against a 2-7 Jets team with RT Spencer Brown doubtful (likely out), CBs Benford and Hancock and S Franklin questionable, and 27 mph gusts. A one-score upset is possible. Inactives are not yet confirmed. If Allen or several of those defensive backs turn up inactive, the leg should be dropped.

checks.team_news: Sunday-morning re-check (inactives not out before 19:35 UTC). No new Sunday report found; the Friday reports still stand (therams.com, azcardinals.com, SI, Yahoo). Rams: QB Matthew Stafford (right elbow) full all week with no designation, so he is expected to start but this is not officially confirmed. Out: G Steve Avila (hamstring, Beaux Limmer likely at left guard) and TE Terrance Ferguson. WR Puka Nacua and WR Davante Adams are on IR, and CB Jaylen Watson is out for the season. Questionable: CB Trent McDuffie (back; did not practise Thursday, limited Friday, missed last week, status depends on Sunday workload; if out, Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace cover), S Kam Curl (toe, no further detail found), OLB Myles Garrett (rest designation; McVay said Friday he expects him to play, though Garrett said 'we're not 100'), TE Davis Allen, LS Joe Cardona. Cardinals: rookie QB Carson Beck is described as the new starter for his NFL debut (ESPN/Yardbarker, SI, Arizona Sports), not yet confirmed by the inactives. Out: C Hjalte Froholdt (concussion), RG Jon Gaines II, DL Zach Carter, WR Michael Wilson. Darius Robinson (wrist) was added to the report. No Sunday downgrade or surprise scratch found for either side.
checks.lineups: Not confirmed. The official inactives are expected about 19:35 UTC (90 minutes before the 21:05 UTC kickoff) and were not out at the time of this check. Expected: Stafford for the Rams with a thin receiver group (Nacua and Adams on IR, rookie CJ Daniels Jr. and Higbee/Atwell/Mumpfield in bigger roles) and Limmer at left guard. Cardinals: Carson Beck at QB behind a line missing its center and right guard. McDuffie, Curl and Garrett remain unconfirmed until the inactives.
checks.rotation: No short week or bye issue found. Rams (5-4) have won 3 straight (Raiders, Chargers, Washington 20-13); Garrett's bye-week comment refers to the Rams' bye after this game. Cardinals (3-6) lost 17-3 at Seattle last week. Venue note: the game is at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, so the Rams are the road team even though the market lists them first. Short in-division trip, no time-zone change.
checks.motivation: Rams 5-4 and tied with Seattle for second in the NFC West, still fighting for a playoff spot (ESPN FPI playoff odds 37.9%), and they want revenge for the Oct 18 loss. Cardinals 3-6 with about 2% playoff odds, a first-year head coach (Mike LaFleur, no change in the last 7 days) and a rookie QB, so they are playing for pride. The favourite has plenty to play for, so the hard no-stakes rule does not apply.
checks.form: Rams: lost to Arizona 16-18 on Oct 18, then beat Las Vegas, the Chargers and Washington 20-13; the offence is thin without Nacua and Adams. Cardinals: lost 3-17 at Seattle, 3-6 overall, with the QB position in turmoil (Minshew out with a UCL injury, Brissett traded), though they scored 18 in the earlier win over the Rams with six Chad Ryland field goals.
checks.h2h: Same-division rivals, so a soft risk. Oct 18 at SoFi: Cardinals won 18-16 on a Ryland 43-yard field goal as time expired, as a 12.5 to 13.5 underdog; the Rams turned the ball over twice in Cardinals territory in the 4th quarter. Rams are 6-4 ATS in the last 10 meetings. Low-scoring, field-goal-driven games. Draw impossible, but variance is high with a total of about 39.5 to 40.
checks.odds: Price check: live Polymarket Rams 80.5% (p_market 0.805) vs 79.5% at first listing (p_first 0.795), a move of +1.3% relative in the Rams' favour, so nothing has moved against the favourite and no unexplained fall. The candidates file had no fresh DraftKings figures this refresh, so the Friday book numbers are the latest I read: DraftKings (via SI) Rams -450 / Cardinals +350, spread -9.5, total 40 (de-vigged about 78.7% Rams); VegasInsider consensus Rams -500 / +380 (about 80.0%), opened -535 / +400 with the spread opened at -10.5 and now -9.5; FanDuel Rams -521 / +400 (about 80.7%). The total fell from 47.5 to 39.5 on injuries and the QB situation. Books and Polymarket agree at about 79-81%.
checks.models: numberFire gives the Rams 73.6% (FanDuel research page), about 7 points below the live market. ESPN power rankings: Rams 12th, Cardinals 25th. ESPN FPI gives the Rams 37.9% to make the playoffs. No DVOA or Elo found. The model gap supports shading p below the market.
checks.venue_weather: State Farm Stadium, Glendale AZ (retractable roof; the Cardinals are the home team). Forecast for kickoff is clear, 72-76F, wind 3-4 mph, 0% precipitation (Covers, footballdb). Roof expected open but not confirmed. Weather is not a factor.

games.reason: Pre-kickoff re-check (Sunday morning, inactives not yet out): nothing new is wrong and the price has moved slightly in the Rams' favour (0.795 to 0.805, +1.3%). Rams are a 9.5-point road favourite over a 3-6 Cardinals side starting rookie QB Carson Beck for the first time, with the Cardinals' center and right guard out, and books and Polymarket agree on about 80%. Confidence stays medium, not high, because the official inactives are not out, so Stafford, McDuffie, Curl and Garrett are unconfirmed, the Rams lack both Nacua and Adams, and the same Cardinals beat them 18-16 three weeks ago. p is shaded 2.5 points below the live market for those reasons and numberFire's lower 73.6%.
games.main_risk: A low-scoring game (total about 40) decided by one score: the Rams' thin receiving group stalls as it did on Oct 18 while divisional familiarity keeps it close. Open items until the inactives: McDuffie (back) or Garrett ruled out, Stafford not officially confirmed, and Beck not officially confirmed as the Cardinals' starter. A downgrade of McDuffie or a surprise Stafford scratch would drop this leg to low.

checks.team_news: Re-check Sunday 16:35 UTC. The official inactives are NOT out yet (due about 19:35 UTC), so nothing is confirmed. Latest reports I could read: Seattle QB Sam Darnold ruled out, Drew Lock expected to start (oblique, Week 9; Macdonald said the exam was good and he expects Lock to play through it); Quenton Nelson out (knee procedure) per search snippets of seahawks.com, Bleacher Report, ABC7. Earlier Friday report (kept from last night): Charles Cross (ankle) and Leonard Williams (stinger) out; Seattle elevated CB Trevon Diggs and T Bobby Hart on Saturday. Raiders: rookie Fernando Mendoza expected to make his first start after Kirk Cousins was traded (search summary, ABC7/TSN); I found no Sunday report that changes this, and no Sunday downgrade for either team. ESPN summary API returned 403, so no ESPN inactives or DraftKings numbers could be read.
checks.lineups: Expected: Lock (SEA) vs Mendoza (LV), neither confirmed by inactives. Seattle line likely without Cross and Nelson (Josh Jones at tackle, Hart elevated). Seattle has the top-ranked defense against a first-time starter; Raiders defense ranked last. Inactives needed before any upgrade.
checks.rotation: No rotation risk. Seattle: Week 9 win over Arizona 17-3, next a Week 12 game vs 49ers. Raiders: lost 38-17 at 49ers, normal rest. Nothing new found.
checks.motivation: Seattle 5-4 and in the playoff hunt, Raiders 4-5; both need the win, no dead-rubber risk, not a rivalry. Unchanged.
checks.form: Seattle: W 17-3 vs ARI behind Lock (19/28, 175 yds, 1 TD), L 17-34 vs CHI before that; defense is the strength, offense below average. Raiders: lost 4 of last 5, defense has allowed 30+ points six straight games. Unchanged.
checks.h2h: Only a betting note: Raiders 3-1 against the spread in the last four meetings; no rivalry. Unchanged.
checks.odds: Polymarket live Seahawks 0.715 vs 0.725 at first listing: -1.4% relative (-1.0 point), under the 3% threshold. The candidates file has no DraftKings/ESPN block, so DraftKings now vs opening could not be compared. Last known (BetMGM via SI, from last night): Seahawks -285 / Raiders +230, spread -6.5, total 40.5; line opened at SEA -3 and moved to -6.5 after the Cousins trade, explained by news. The small Polymarket dip has no new news explaining it, but is minor.
checks.models: ESPN FPI: Seattle 73.9% by 6.4 points; numberFire 70% Seattle; power rankings Seattle No. 6-7, Raiders No. 23 (from the morning research, not re-fetched).
checks.venue_weather: Allegiant Stadium, Las Vegas, enclosed climate-controlled dome: no weather risk. Venue is the Raiders' home; the file's 'home' label (Seahawks) is just the first-named team. Kickoff 21:05 UTC.

games.reason: Seahawks to win stays a clear market favourite (live 0.715, about 71% de-vigged earlier) with FPI 73.9% and the top defense against a rookie QB making his first start. Confidence stays medium, not high: the official inactives are not out, so Lock (oblique), Mendoza's start and the Seattle line (Cross and Nelson out) are unconfirmed. The price dipped 1.4% (0.725 to 0.715), below the 3% drop line, and no Sunday news was found that hurts Seattle. Estimate kept at 0.69, a little under the market, because of the backup QB and patched line. Re-check after the 19:35 UTC inactives before upgrading.
games.main_risk: Seattle offense stalls with backup QB Lock (oblique) behind a patched line (Cross and Nelson out) in a 40.5-total game, so a Raiders upset stays plausible; a late Lock inactive or a Sunday surprise would make this low.

checks.team_news: No withdrawal or injury report found for either player in tonight's searches. The only withdrawal in the field is Jannik Sinner (knee), and Alex de Minaur and Taylor Fritz are the alternates. Zverev is the No 1 seed and Jodar the No 8 seed. Jodar qualified on 7 Nov after Alcaraz beat Fritz in the Paris Masters quarterfinal, and this is his ATP Finals debut. No fitness comments from either player could be found, so that stays unverified.
checks.lineups: Tennismajors and nittoatpfinals.com both list the order of play for Sun 15 Nov at the Inalpi Arena, Turin. Zverev vs Jodar is the 2pm CET singles match (13:00 UTC), after the 11:30 doubles. Shelton vs Fils follows not before 8:30pm. This is a schedule from the press, not an ATP-confirmed order of play posted tonight. No withdrawal or walkover is announced.
checks.rotation: This is the opening day of the round robin, so neither player has a match this week yet. Both are coming from the Paris Masters. Both opening matches are on the same indoor hard court. Neither next match is a concern for this game.
checks.motivation: John McEnroe Group: Zverev (1), Shelton (3), Fils (6), Jodar (8). This is match 1 of 3 for both players, so nobody is qualified or eliminated and there is no dead rubber. Both want the win to start well. Zverev will also face Shelton later in the group. A debutant opponent with nothing to lose is a soft risk only.
checks.form: Last 6-10 results for either player could not be verified tonight, so none are stated. Zverev is world No 1 in the 2026 Race and a two-time champion here (2018, 2021).
